title: Dispatch OGF 5: One Fruit Shows an Empty Evacuation Street
summary: The orchard offers a route that no official plan has drawn.
author: Clara Vale, Staff Correspondent
paragraphs: Among the scenes of crowded flight, Dr. Saye has found a single pear showing North Loom Street empty at 4:12. The windows are closed and the paving is dry. Its viewpoint is the upper room of a boarding house whose tenant, a young woman named Nell Armitage, has not yet received notice to leave.

In another fruit from the same branch, Miss Armitage is seen helping six children into a cart on the flooded street. She says she does not know the children. Mrs. Rill recognized one as the son of a worker who lives beside the reservoir. The different scenes cannot both describe the same moment in a single course of events.

“That is the first useful thing they have told us,” said Inspector Voss. If the street is empty because the people have already moved, the city may be able to choose that course. He has marked the street as a priority in a draft evacuation plan.

Dr. Saye has recorded the position of every fruit on the western branch. Those showing water hang nearest the trunk. The dry street is near its tip. She thinks the scenes shift as the root system grows. Mrs. Rill has asked that the fruit not be used as a map until the city has checked every route on foot.

Engineers began lowering the reservoir yesterday. Its level fell as intended, but the glass threads in the drainage channel widened overnight. The city will begin voluntary relocation of the lowest streets tomorrow morning.
